articles.title: Mulher recebeu US$ 5 mil para se mudar para cidade pequena dos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Programas de incentivo à mudança oferecem apoio a quem quer deixar as grandes cidades em busca de uma vida mais barata e tranquila.
articles.summary: Programas de incentivo à mudança oferecem apoio a quem quer deixar as grandes cidades em busca de uma vida mais barata e tranquila.
articles.body:
Brianna Beyrouti diz que se mudar para uma região mais barata dos EUA permitiu que ela levasse os filhos para viajar nas férias — Foto: BBC

Ao lembrar da vida que levava em Portland, no estado de Oregon, nos Estados Unidos , Brianna Beyrouti diz que estava se "afogando" financeiramente.

"Eu vivia de salário em salário. Toda vez que surgia um imprevisto, era aquela coisa: 'Meus Deus, as crianças precisam de sapatos, como vou pagar por isso?'. Como mãe solo, tudo fica nas minhas costas."

No ano passado, Beyrouti deixou Portland e sua região metropolitana, que tem 2,5 milhões de habitantes.

Ela e os dois filhos se mudaram cerca de 3,2 mil km para o leste, para Muncie, no estado de Indiana , uma cidade de 65 mil habitantes com universidade e muitas áreas abertas. A mudança foi feita com a ajuda de um programa que ofereceu US$ 5 mil (cerca de R$ 25,7 mil) para ajudar nos custos de transferência e atrair novos moradores.

A mudança transformou a situação financeira de Beyrouti. Ela continua trabalhando remotamente para o mesmo banco e, por isso, mantém o salário anual de US$ 107 mil (aproximadamente R$ 550 mil). Mas conseguiu comprar uma casa pela primeira vez e hoje gasta menos com o financiamento do imóvel do que gastava antes com aluguel.

Em Portland, ela desembolsava US$ 1.290 (em torno de R$ 6,6 mil) por mês de aluguel de um apartamento. Em Muncie, a soma da prestação da casa, do seguro residencial e do imposto sobre a propriedade chega a US$ 1,1 mil (cerca de R$ 5.650) mensais.

Além disso, o imposto estadual sobre a renda é menor em Indiana, e Beyrouti passou a gastar menos com seguro do carro e contas de energia. No total, ela diz que hoje lhe sobram US$ 600 (cerca de R$ 3,1 mil) a mais por mês.

"Consigo aproveitar mais a vida do que antes", diz Beyrouti. "Quando meus filhos querem alguma coisa, hoje tenho muito mais condições de dizer sim. Minha qualidade de vida melhorou muito."

Beyrouti não é a única a trocar uma cidade grande por outra menor.

Com o custo de vida ainda pesando no bolso dos americanos, algumas das maiores cidades do país têm perdido moradores em busca de lugares onde a moradia seja mais barata.

Um relatório de 2025 da Associação Nacional de Corretores de Imóveis dos EUA constatou que, entre as pessoas que se mudaram para outro estado americano, o custo de vida foi o principal motivo da mudança.

Nos últimos anos, cidades como Nova York, Los Angeles e Portland registraram queda na população. O movimento também foi impulsionado pela maior aceitação do trabalho remoto desde a pandemia de covid-19.

Na direção oposta, algumas cidades menores dos EUA, como Muncie, voltaram a ganhar moradores depois de décadas de queda populacional — e dão suporte a essa tendência para fomentar a economia local.

No ano passado, Muncie chegou a 65.466 habitantes, segundo dados oficiais. Eram 65.194 em 2020, mas o número ainda está bem abaixo dos 71.828 registrados em 1990.

Para se destacar entre outras cidades e atrair trabalhadores remotos de fora de Indiana, a prefeitura de Muncie oferece US$ 5 mil em dinheiro para ajudar nos custos da mudança.

O incentivo é oferecido por meio do site MakeMyMove, que reúne vários programas semelhantes oferecidos por pequenas cidades e municípios dos EUA. Esses locais pagam uma taxa de assinatura à plataforma.

Entre outros benefícios oferecidos a possíveis novos moradores estão ingressos de cinema gratuitos, tíquetes para restaurantes e até garrafas de vinho gratuitas.

Brianna e os filhos trocaram Portland por Muncie, cidade de 65 mil habitantes — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Beyrouti e os filhos estão entre cerca de 100 famílias que se mudaram para Muncie por meio do programa. Beyrouti, aliás, diz que nunca tinha ouvido falar da cidade.

Em todo o país, o MakeMyMove afirma ter ajudado 1.000 pessoas a se mudar no ano passado e e prevê elevar esse número para 1.500 em 2026.

A cientista Elena Chrysostomou também recorreu a um programa de incentivo para trocar uma cidade grande por uma pequena. Em 2024, ela deixou San Diego, cidade na Califórnia cuja região metropolitana tem mais de 3 milhões de habitantes, e se mudou para Jacksonville, uma cidade de 17,7 mil habitantes na zona rural do Estado de Illinois (cuja maior cidade é Chicago).

A mudança teve apoio da Jacksonville Regional Economic Development Corporation (Corporação para o Desenvolvimento Econômico Regional de Jacksonville, em tradução livre), que ofereceu US$ 5 mil (cerca de R$ 25,7 mil) em dinheiro, além de um "pacote de qualidade de vida" avaliado em US$ 4 mil (aproximadamente R$ 20,6 mil), com academia gratuita e passes para jogar golfe.

A corporação afirma que, embora a região "já seja um ótimo lugar para viver", o programa ajuda a "tornar a oferta [de transferência] mais atraente".

Chrysostomou gastava US$ 3 mil (em torno de R$ 15,4 mil) por mês no aluguel de um apartamento de um quarto em San Diego. Hoje, é dona de uma casa de três quartos e paga US$ 1.868 (cerca de R$ 9.600) por mês de financiamento imobiliário.

Ao mesmo tempo, seu salário aumentou 22% depois que mudou de emprego, e o trajeto até o trabalho caiu de 15 minutos de carro para apenas um minuto . "Nunca achei que conseguiria comprar uma casa sozinha. Sempre pensei que precisaria de um parceiro e, mesmo assim, em San Diego seria muito difícil", diz Chrysostomou.

"Tenho mais liberdade. Há mais segurança e independência."

Mudar-se para Jacksonville, em Illinois, permitiu que Elena Chrysostomou comprasse uma casa — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Embora nem ela nem Beyrouti se arrependam da mudança, as duas reconhecem algumas desvantagens na nova rotina. Entre elas estão a menor oferta de atividades e restaurantes, a distância de amigos e familiares e, no caso de Beyrouti, a dificuldade de adaptar os filhos às novas escolas.

Em Portland, Beyrouti gostava de ir a pé a parques e lojas. Agora, depende do carro para praticamente tudo.

Ainda assim, diz estar muito satisfeita. "Tenho a maior reserva de dinheiro que já consegui juntar na vida, sou dona da minha casa e posso fazer coisas com meus filhos. Nós até viajamos de férias pela primeira vez na vida do meu caçula."

Impacto de nômades digitais em cidades pequenas

Esse processo de mudança de moradores de cidades grandes para pequenas, que alguns classificam como uma expulsão dessas pessoas, não acontece apenas nos EUA.

Mesmo com o fim da pandemia de covid-19, muitas pessoas continuam trabalhando remotamente ou investiram para valer no modo de vida nômade também na América latina.

Muitas deles são remuneradas em moeda valorizada (como o dólar em relação ao real) ou mesmo com salários de cidades ou Estados mais ricos e procuram cidades mais baratas, com qualidade de vida para morar ou passar longas temporadas, de acordo com Diana Quintas, sócia da Fragomen no Brasil, empresa especializada em imigração e líder na área de mobilidade internacional de pessoas físicas e empresas.

"Falando de nomadismo digital na América Latina, nossa região é escolhida por muitos profissionais porque juntamos qualidade de vida a um custo atrativo para os mais bem colocados no mercado", diz a especialista.

Porém, isso afeta diretamente no aumento dos aluguéis para quem reside naquele lugar, aponta Isadora Guerreiro, coordenadora do Lab Cidade da Faculdade de Arquitetura e Urbanismo da Universidade de São Paulo (FAU-USP).

Esse processo, conhecido como gentrificação, se dá pela transformação da população local, que é substituída por outros perfis de renda mais alta, contribuindo para a supervalorização de um bairro ou cidade e, consequentemente, para a expulsão de antigos moradores.

Segundo Guerreiro, esse movimento aprofunda a desigualdade urbana.

"O que estamos vivendo na América Latina é que esses proprietários corporativos, que são empresas ou fundos de investimento internacional, passam a ser donos de unidades (...) e passam a definir (preços) baseado no setor internacional. (...) É totalmente descolado de quanto as pessoas podem pagar. Isso vai redefinindo o bairro", diz Guerreiro.

Reportagem adicional de Priscila Carvalho

articles.title: Pedágio sobe e Campos pede antecipação de obras na BR-101 | G1
articles.standfirst: Município quer revisão do cronograma de intervenções após aumento do pedágio para R$ 10,80.
articles.summary: Município quer revisão do cronograma de intervenções após aumento do pedágio para R$ 10,80.
articles.body:
Prefeitura aponta obras consideradas como prioritárias para melhorar o trânsito em Campos — Foto: Divulgação

A Prefeitura de Campos dos Goytacazes , no Norte Fluminense, pediu à Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT) a revisão do cronograma de obras previstas no novo contrato de concessão da BR-101. O município quer antecipar intervenções consideradas prioritárias.

O pedido foi encaminhado depois do reajuste da tarifa do pedágio. Desde 9 de setembro, a cobrança na praça de Campos passou para R$ 10,80, um aumento de mais de 40%.

Entre os pedidos estão a duplicação das faixas de tráfego entre os quilômetros 64,1 e 65,5 (trecho que compreende a região entre a Rua Rocha Leão e o Partage Shopping), a antecipação da implantação de multivia entre os quilômetros 67 e 70 e a priorização da multivia no sentido Norte.

A Prefeitura também solicitou um estudo técnico e jurídico para avaliar a integração ao sistema operacional da concessão de um trecho urbano de aproximadamente dois quilômetros atualmente utilizado como parte do fluxo correspondente à pista Sul da BR-101. A área inclui a Avenida Estilac Leal, nas proximidades do km 62,2, e a Rua Espírito Santo, até a região do km 64,1.

De acordo com o cronograma atual, a elaboração do projeto do contorno de Campos está prevista para começar a partir do oitavo ano da concessão.

A Prefeitura considera o prazo distante e afirma que as principais intervenções necessárias para reduzir os impactos da BR-101 na área urbana não estão previstas para os próximos três anos.

“O novo contrato que começou em março não prevê, nos próximos três anos pelo menos, nenhuma obra, nenhum investimento que venham a reduzir os impactos do trânsito da rodovia no dia a dia da cidade. O prefeito está pedindo, inclusive sugerindo algumas modificações no cronograma, que praticamente não iriam impactar o custo contratual”, explicou o subsecretário de Mobilidade, Sérgio Mansur.

O que pode ser feito para antecipar as obras?

Para o especialista em Direito Público Gabriel Rangel, a ANTT possui mecanismos regulatórios que podem permitir mudanças no cronograma. Ele afirma, porém, que a antecipação depende de questões relacionadas aos projetos, às licenças ambientais e à definição dos custos.

“O campista já está pagando R$ 10,80 hoje, depois da rodovia ter acumulado mais de R$ 372 milhões em excedente tarifário cobrado sem investimento”, afirmou Rangel.

Segundo o especialista, a regulação permite a revisão do fluxo e o uso do chamado fluxo de caixa marginal. Para ele, antes da execução das obras é necessário destravar projetos e licenças ambientais e estabelecer como será financiada a antecipação prevista no contrato.

“Tem [ferramentas para antecipar o cronograma]. A regulação permite a revisão do fluxo e o uso de fluxo de caixa marginal, mas existem duas condições. Primeiro, destravar os projetos e as licenças ambientais, sem as quais nenhuma máquina entra na pista. Segundo, definir a conta financeira dessa antecipação do contrato”, explicou.

Além das intervenções diretamente relacionadas à BR-101, a Prefeitura estuda alternativas para ampliar a mobilidade entre diferentes regiões do município.

Uma das propostas é a implantação de uma nova via de ligação entre Travessão e Ururaí utilizando o antigo leito ferroviário, atualmente desativado. Segundo Sérgio Mansur, o anteprojeto prevê pistas de rolamento e ciclofaixas.

A proposta também considera, em uma etapa futura, a possibilidade de implantação de um sistema de transporte coletivo de maior capacidade, como um veículo leve sobre trilhos.

A Prefeitura informou que aguarda uma manifestação da ANTT sobre o pedido de revisão do cronograma de intervenções da concessão.

articles.title: Aposta única do Paraná acerta a quina da Mega-Sena e é premiada; veja a cidade e valor | G1
articles.standfirst: Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio acumulou em R$ 102 milhões. O próximo sorteio será realizado nesta quinta-feira (17).
articles.summary: Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio acumulou em R$ 102 milhões. O próximo sorteio será realizado nesta quinta-feira (17).
articles.body:
No Paraná, uma única aposta acertou cinco dos seis números sorteados para a Mega-Sena no sorteio desta terça-feira (15) e levou a premiação da faixa da quina: R$ 53.305,58.

Ela foi feita na lotérica Zebrinha da Sorte, em Ponta Grossa , nos Campos Gerais, e custou R$ 6.

🍀 Os números sorteados neste concurso 3058 foram: 14 - 23 - 53 - 56 - 57 - 60.

No total, 49 apostas brasileiras acertaram a quina. O sorteio também premiou 3.632 apostas na quadra; cada uma ganhou R$ 1.185,42.

Nenhuma aposta acertou todos os seis números, e por isso o prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 102 milhões para o próximo sorteio . Ele será realizado nesta quinta (17).

Foto ilustrativa — Foto: Millena Sartori/g1

A Mega-Sena tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, às quintas e aos domingos.

📶 É possível apostar em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet, no internet banking da Caixa Econômica Federal ou no site ou app das Loterias Caixa , que podem ser acessados por celular, computador ou outros dispositivos.

🔞 Para concorrer, é necessário ter mais que 18 anos de idade.

💰A aposta mínima, de 6 números, custa R$ 6. Quanto mais números marcar, maior o preço da aposta e mais chances de faturar.

articles.title: Após forte chuva, granizo deixa estragos, falta de luz e de água no Sul de Minas | G1
articles.standfirst: Queda de árvores, danos em estruturas e interrupções no abastecimento mobilizam equipes nesta quarta-feira (16).
articles.summary: Queda de árvores, danos em estruturas e interrupções no abastecimento mobilizam equipes nesta quarta-feira (16).
articles.body:
Moradores e equipes de serviços públicos seguem trabalhando nesta quarta-feira (16) para reparar os estragos provocados pelo temporal que atingiu cidades do Sul de Minas na terça-feira (15). A combinação de chuva forte, granizo e ventos causou queda de árvores, danos em estruturas, falta de energia elétrica e problemas no abastecimento de água em diversos municípios da região.

Em Três Corações , a chuva começou por volta das 16h e durou cerca de 30 minutos, segundo a Defesa Civil. O temporal provocou danos em diferentes pontos da cidade e deixou moradores sem energia elétrica. A falta de eletricidade também afetou o abastecimento de água em parte do município.

Em Varginha , o granizo atingiu diversos bairros e, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), os ventos chegaram a 72 km/h. Moradores registraram alagamentos e acúmulo de pedras de gelo em quintais e ruas, situação que ainda podia ser observada horas após a chuva. A prefeitura mobilizou equipes de limpeza urbana para recolher galhos e sujeiras.

São Lourenço (MG) está entre as cidades mais impactadas pela queda de granizo — Foto: Reprodução / São Lourenço Jornal e Canal Potência

Em São Lourenço , a chuva forte e o granizo também atingiram diferentes pontos do município durante a tarde. A Defesa Civil fez vistorias para verificar possíveis danos, enquanto moradores relataram interrupções no fornecimento de energia.

Os reflexos da tempestade também foram registrados na BR-460, rodovia que liga São Lourenço a Lambari. Segundo a Defesa Civil de Carmo de Minas , a rodovia ficou obstruída e equipes da Defesa Civil, com apoio da Polícia Militar, trabalharam na retirada das árvores. Não houve registro de feridos.

Reflexos da tempestade na BR-460, rodovia que liga São Lourenço a Lambari e passa por Carmo de Minas — Foto: Defesa Civil de Carmo de Minas

Em Delfinópolis , a chuva forte acompanhada de granizo provocou danos em casas, telhados e estruturas, além da queda de árvores e galhos. Segundo a prefeitura, não houve vítimas. Na entrada da cidade, fios se enrolaram e pegaram fogo. A Cemig foi acionada e restabeleceu ainda na noite de terça-feira a energia em pontos afetados. Alguns bananais foram afetados, mas ainda não há estimativa das perdas.

Delfinópolis (MG) teve chuva forte acompanhada de granizo — Foto: Prefeitura de Delfinópolis

Em São Tomé das Letras , a chuva forte acompanhada de ventos e granizo atingiu o município por volta das 16h, principalmente a região rural de Pontinha. A Defesa Civil foi acionada para retirar galhos que caíram sobre o asfalto. Não houve registro de alagamentos, danos ou feridos.

Em Paraguaçu , o granizo foi registrado na zona rural de Água Branca, às margens da Represa de Furnas. Na área urbana, houve chuva, mas sem ocorrência de granizo.

Já em Três Pontas , a chuva forte atingiu principalmente a zona rural. Até o momento, não foram registrados transtornos no município.

Os efeitos do temporal também atingiram o fornecimento de energia elétrica em diferentes cidades do Sul de Minas. Em Três Corações, o mapa de ocorrências da Cemig chegou a apontar mais de 950 unidades consumidoras sem energia. Em São Lourenço, eram cerca de 300, e em Delfinópolis, aproximadamente 120.

Segundo a Cemig, a maior parte dos clientes afetados pela chuva já teve o fornecimento restabelecido e não há grandes blocos de consumidores sem energia. Em Carmo de Minas, a situação estava praticamente normalizada. Em Delfinópolis, os atendimentos se concentravam principalmente na área rural. Em São Lourenço, os bairros Centro e Várzea registravam o maior número de ocorrências. Em Três Corações, os maiores volumes estavam em Vila Jessé e São Conrado.

A companhia informou que a normalização do serviço deve ocorrer gradualmente ao longo desta quarta-feira (16). A orientação é que os clientes registrem ocorrências pelos canais de atendimento da empresa, pelo telefone 116 ou pelo aplicativo Cemig Atende.

A falta de energia também afetou o abastecimento de água em Três Corações. Segundo a Copasa, o fornecimento pode apresentar intermitência até que o serviço de energia seja restabelecido. A normalização deve ocorrer de forma gradual depois da retomada do fornecimento elétrico.

Entre as áreas que podem ser afetadas estão Centro, Cidade Jardim, Jardim América, Vila Jessé, São Conrado, Vila Mariana, Vila Militar, Parque São José, Santana, Nova Três Corações I e Nova Três Corações II, além de outras localidades urbanas e rurais. Segundo a Copasa, imóveis que possuem caixa-d'água podem não sofrer impactos no abastecimento.

articles.title: In December 2019, Australia unveiled a 4-meter underwater statue that glows with real-time ocean temperature data from a Great Barrier Reef monitoring station
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Explore Australia's Ocean Siren, a stunning 4-meter statue in Townsville that changes colors based on real-time ocean temperature data from the Great Barrier Reef, raising awareness of coral bleaching and marine sustainability.
articles.body: Ocean Siren, an illuminated sculpture standing four meters tall, can be found at the Strand jetty in Townsville, Queensland, though the name 'underwater' may mislead many into thinking that it is underwater. It rises out of shallow foreshore waters, visible above the surface at any time of day. What the sculpture does share with a genuine underwater installation is its purpose: its LED lights change color continuously, reflecting live sea temperature readings pulled from a Great Barrier Reef monitoring station. It was unveiled in December 2019, according to the Museum of Underwater Art’s official site.The sculpture was modeled on a local Wulgurukaba girlThe Ocean Siren sculpture was designed by British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor in partnership with James Cook University and the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), according to the Museum of Underwater Art's website. It was created as a tribute to Takoda Johnson, an Indigenous custodian of the site and a 12-year-old girl from the Wulgurukaba community. Ocean Siren was the first installation created for the Museum of Underwater Art (MOUA), a non-profit foundation established by the Australian and Queensland governments.The statue draws its data from the Davies Reef weather stationThe Ocean Siren is made of stainless steel, which has been joined by welding, together with the help of translucent acrylic with 202 LEDs, which get power from the energy generated through the use of solar panels. The color of these lights varies from dark blue to dark red depending upon the temperature recorded through the weather station at Davies Reef, which is one of the numerous weather stations set up by AIMS since 1987 in the Great Barrier Reef region.Coral bleaching research shows why this kind of monitoring mattersThese color changes reflect temperature increases linked to recurrent mass bleaching events in the reef. The results of the paper published in Nature and titled ‘Global warming and recurrent mass bleaching of corals’ indicate that the degree and the geographical distribution of the bleaching event in 1998, 2002 and 2016 corresponded closely with the distribution of increased sea surface temperatures during those years. What made 2016 a unique case is the fact that local water quality and local fisheries had little impact on the bleaching distribution, while the previous bleaching events did not provide any protection against bleaching. The authors suggest that reducing warming is essential to limiting future bleaching events.Public art has a measurable role in raising awareness of ocean issuesTaylor himself has stated that his purpose for designing Ocean Siren was to bring attention to the changes occurring underwater, which are rarely experienced first-hand by anyone. This concept is supported by scientific research, since a systematic review published in Cambridge Prisms: Coastal Futures titled ‘The Role of Art in Coastal and Marine Sustainability’ showed that the viewers of the environmental art were more likely to increase their awareness of the problems in the coastal and marine areas, as well as show their engagement with the topic later on. In the review, the researchers screened 1,352 articles from Scopus and Web of Science and selected 79 papers out of those, only 19 of which were impact measurement articles. According to the review, visual art was represented by 40% of the dataset, while engagement was the most prevalent outcome sought out by the artists.Ocean Siren was not the only installation at the Museum of Underwater Art. Another, called Coral Greenhouse, followed in 2020. It is located at a depth of about 16 to 18 meters at John Brewer Reef, which is an approximate distance of two hours' boat ride from Townsville. Such information was taken from the Museum of Underwater Art webpage. Contrary to the previous sculpture, this installation was developed from pH-neutral concrete and stainless steel.The project reflects a broader shift toward data-driven environmental artAccording to the review of Cambridge Prisms, environmental art normally affects the perception of people indirectly through pictures and symbols rather than the actual data. In this case, this particular art is different from other environmental art since Ocean Siren does not have an indirect means of affecting people's perception, but rather it is the transformation of a real measurement from the device into a visible symbol for the people.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Man acquitted after spray painting Sir Winston Churchill statue
articles.summary: Caspar San Giorgio, 39, is found not guilty of criminal damage following a trial at Southwark Crown Court.
articles.body:
A man who spray-painted slogans on to a statue of Sir Winston Churchill has been found not guilty of criminal damage.

Caspar San Giorgi, who is also known as Olax Outis, climbed on to the statue in Parliament Square on 27 February.

He was accused of causing more than £7,000 of damage by using red spray paint to cover the statue with phrases including "Stop the Genocide" and "Free Palestine", describing Churchill as a "Zionist war criminal".

San Giorgi, 39, was acquitted at Southwark Crown Court on Monday afternoon following a trial, a court official said.

During the trial, he told a jury he did not believe he had done anything criminal because he was sending a message to Parliament, and he disputed that the washable paint had actually damaged the statue.

The court previously heard that San Giorgi went to Parliament Square just before 4:00 GMT, carrying cans of spray paint and a ladder to climb the plinth.

He removed his coat to reveal a red boiler suit with the words "I support Palestine Action" on the back, and "set about defacing the statue – spraying… the words Free Palestine and red triangles on the front, and Never Again Is Now on the rear", said prosecutor Peter Ratliff.

San Giorgi had told the jury: "Whether you convict me or not is not too much of a concern for me.

"Whether I get acquitted, deported, imprisoned for years, I can be proud of having spoken about injustice and I have accounted for my actions.

San Giorgi was seen painting the statue by a heritage warden for the Greater London Authority, who alerted police.

In the immediate aftermath of the incident, a Downing Street spokesperson called the defacing of the statue "completely abhorrent", adding: "Churchill was a great Briton."

articles.title: In 2007, a New York family’s $3 garage-sale bowl became a $2.2M fortune after experts uncovered its 1,000-year-old identity in 2013
articles.summary: US News: In 2013, a family's $3 garage-sale find turned out to be a rare 1,000-year-old Chinese Ding bowl that sold for $2.2 million at Sotheby's auction, revealing the astonishing journey from an ordinary living room to global art fame.
articles.body: A small white bowl was bought for $3 at a New York state garage sale in 2007, and sat in a family's living room for years. In 2013, experts identified it as a rare Chinese Ding bowl from the Northern Song dynasty. Sotheby's estimated it at $200,000 to $300,000, and at auction, a London dealer paid $2.225 million including commission. It came from a garage or tag sale where the buyers paid no more than $3. They took it home and kept it on display, and were apparently unaware that the plain-looking bowl dated to a period roughly 1,000 years earlier.Experts examined the object and identified the ceramic as Ding ware, a type of Chinese porcelain that is associated with the Northern Song dynasty, which ruled from 960 to 1127. A contemporary report by the Los Angeles Times said the bowl was about five inches across and had an ivory-colored glaze with carved decoration. Sotheby's had placed a pre-sale estimate of $200,000 to $300,000 on it.A bowl from the Northern Song dynastyDing ware was known for its thinly potted bodies and pale glaze, and the bowl found in New York belonged to a recognized ceramic tradition whose surviving examples are held by major museums and collectors. The Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection includes Northern Song Ding ware dating to the 11th and 12th centuries. The museum describes its own example as porcelain with an incised design beneath an ivory-white glaze and identifies it as Ding ware from China. The Met also makes images of many of its collection objects available for unrestricted commercial and noncommercial use through its Open Access program.That context helps explain why specialists valued the garage-sale bowl so highly, as its age was only part of the story. The form, decoration, material and glaze placed it within a closely studied category of Chinese ceramics. Contemporary accounts said Sotheby's knew of only one other bowl with the same form, size and almost identical decoration, and that example was in the British Museum in London. The auction house's estimate already reflected the object's rarity, but the eventual sale price went far beyond it.The auction changed the value of a $3 purchaseOn March 19, 2013, the bowl went under the hammer in New York as part of a Sotheby's sale of Chinese ceramics and works of art, with the successful bidder being Giuseppe Eskenazi, a London dealer and specialist in Chinese art. The final price was $2.225 million including commission, according to contemporary reports. The sale price was more than seven times Sotheby's high estimate and hundreds of thousands of times what the family had paid for it at the garage sale.Reuters' account, republished by the Bangor Daily News, said the unnamed New York family had bought the Ding bowl for no more than $3 in 2007 and displayed it on a mantelpiece without knowing its value, and after experts examined it, the family consigned it for auction.The bowl measured just over five inches across, yet its combination of age, workmanship, rarity and documented similarities to a museum-held example put it in a completely different category from the ordinary household objects surrounding it at the garage sale.The sellers remained anonymous, as did the circumstances that had brought a Northern Song ceramic into a New York garage sale in the first place. The object had been worth $3 when they found it in 2007 for the buyers, and six years later, after expert examination established its identity and provenance, it sold at auction for $2.225 million.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: E.U. chief wants Canada to become the bloc’s 1st associate member
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Wednesday that she wants to open the door for Canada to become the European Union’s first associate member.
articles.body: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Wednesday that she wants to open the door for Canada to become the European Union’s first associate member. The overture comes as Trump’s tariffs and repeated talk of making Canada the 51st state have pushed Ottawa to seek closer economic and security ties with Europe. Carney has called for a “unique alliance” with the EU as Canada seeks to reduce its heavy dependence on U.S. trade. “I would like to work with you on opening the door for Canada being the first associate member of the EU,” von der Leyen told Carney during her annual State of the European Union address. Carney received a standing ovation from European lawmakers. He is due to address the European Parliament on Thursday. Von der Leyen said Canada and the EU would build on their existing free trade agreement, known as CETA, with a broader “Alliance for the Future” aimed at creating “a common prosperity and economic security space.” She cast that closer relationship as rooted not just in trade but in shared democratic values. “Above all, dear Mark, Europe and Canada believe in democracy,” von der Leyen said. “We believe that power does not belong to the strongest, the richest or the loudest, but to all of us. That democracies have the freedom to choose with whom to work.” Von der Leyen said the expanded partnership would cover advanced manufacturing, technology, defense production, the Arctic, energy, critical minerals, batteries, artificial intelligence, quantum computing, cybersecurity and economic security. “This is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength,” she said. “In short, we want to bring the relationship with Canada to the highest level possible.”

articles.title: Police detain dozens at Istanbul protest over LGBTQ+ crackdown
articles.summary: Police on Tuesday detained dozens of demonstrators who staged a protest outside a courthouse in Istanbul to demand the release of LGBTQ+ activists taken into custody during a sweeping crackdown days earlier.
articles.body: Police on Tuesday detained dozens of demonstrators who staged a protest outside a courthouse in Istanbul to demand the release of LGBTQ+ activists taken into custody during a sweeping crackdown days earlier. Police surrounded the demonstrators outside the Caglayan courthouse before detaining them. On Sunday, Turkish authorities cracked down on multiple LGBTQ+ groups and individuals, detaining dozens of members, breaking into association offices and raiding popular hangouts. The organizations’ websites were also blocked. The crackdown aimed to “protect children, the institution of the family, and public order,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said. He said the operation, dubbed “My Family is Safe,” targeted 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses. On Tuesday, Michael O’Flaherty, the Strasbourg, France-based Council of Europe’s Commissioner for Human Rights, expressed concerns over the raids and detentions, saying “mere references to ‘family values’ or ‘protection of children’ cannot serve as legal justification for human rights restrictions.” “I call on the Turkish authorities to release anyone detained for engaging in human rights or civil society work,” he said in a statement, adding that he would continue to monitor the situation. Outside the courthouse, demonstrators carried banners reading: “Being LGBT+ and organizing is not a crime” and chanted slogans in support of LGBTQ+ rights before police intervened. “We are going through a period where there is an attempt by the ruling power to portray LGBT+ people as the cause of every problem in this society,” 36-year old Banu Aslan, one of the protesters, told The Associated Press. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling party, which has roots in Turkey’s Islamic movement, has been increasingly vocal against LGBTQ+ groups in a bid to consolidate the more conservative elements of its base. In 2015, it banned Istanbul Pride, which had tens of thousands of attendees in previous years. Since then, authorities have violently dispersed any attempted gatherings for Pride. This summer, an LGBTQ+ cruise ship that tours the Mediterranean and has docked in Turkey multiple times in the past was refused permission to dock there.

articles.title: War-damaged Gaza building collapses, killing 20 people and trapping nearly 100
articles.summary: Gaza rescuers on Wednesday combed through the wreckage of a bombed-out apartment building that collapsed overnight, killing at least 20 Palestinians, including six children, and trapping dozens of others beneath the rubble.
articles.body: Gaza rescuers on Wednesday combed through the wreckage of a bombed-out apartment building that collapsed overnight, killing at least 20 Palestinians, including six children, and trapping dozens of others beneath the rubble. The incident highlights the ongoing danger for tens of thousands of Palestinians who live in an estimated 2,000 buildings damaged by Israeli airstrikes across Gaza. Rescue workers said 14 others were injured when the seven-story building collapsed. Nearly 100 more people were believed to be trapped under the rubble. A video obtained by Reuters showed rescue workers trying to pull out two people from under a collapsed wall. Another video circulated on social media showed Gaza‘s civil defense spokesperson, Mahmoud Basal, carrying a little girl, wrapped in a blood-stained scarf, in his hands. Raed Al-Dahshan, the director of Gaza City’s civil defense service, said at least 10 families lived in the collapsed building and there was still hope of finding survivors. “We are still hearing voices from under the rubble, so there is still hope to find people,” Dahshan said. Alessandro Mrakic, head of the United Nations Development Programme’s Gaza office, said rescuers from some U.N. agencies were taking part in the rescue efforts, which he described as difficult due to the lack of proper machinery. Egypt’s relief agency was also taking part in rescue efforts. “The situation, as you see, is tragic because we don’t have the equipment and machinery that is needed. So there are actually people that are digging with their bare hands. We need to prepare (for more deaths),” Mrakic said. “There are approximately 400 buildings at risk of collapse. And we know that these buildings will collapse, especially now with the upcoming winter,” he added. Palestinian and U.N. officials blame Israel’s restrictions on Gaza for the lack of heavy machinery in the territory. Israel says its curbs aim to keep equipment out of the hands of militant groups. “Today’s tragedy underscores the grave risks faced by families living ‌in these ⁠structures and the urgent need for safer alternatives. No one should have to risk their life simply to find a safe place to shelter,” said Ramiz Alakbarov, the U.N. humanitarian coordinator for the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Israel’s devastating assault on Gaza — launched after Hamas’ deadly raid into Israel in October 2023 — has generated around 61 million tons of wreckage and debris that could take seven years to clear, according to the U.​N. Dahshan warned residents to stay away from wrecked buildings due to the risk of collapse. The local rescue service says about 2,000 damaged buildings are inhabited by families. “The limited availability of shelter options forced residents to move into this building, believing it was safe. However, at one point it collapsed entirely, tragically crashing down on people as they slept,” Dahshan said. Many families have told Reuters in the past months that they resorted to living in partially damaged buildings to protect themselves against wind and rainstorms, and because of the lack of new tents for the homeless. An October 2025, U.S.-backed ceasefire halted large-scale fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended Israeli strikes and there has been little progress on steps toward permanent peace. Hamas accuses Israel of violating the ceasefire and undermining efforts to implement President Donald Trump’s broader plan to end the Gaza conflict, which includes an Israeli withdrawal from the Gaza Strip and the disarmament of Hamas. Israel says Hamas has been violating the deal. On Tuesday, Israeli airstrikes on a vehicle killed at least two Palestinians, one a child, and wounded seven others in what appeared to be a double tap strike in the northern Gaza Strip neighborhood of Sheikh Radwan, according to medics. The Israeli military said it had struck a militant in the area, without elaborating, and separately that it struck a Hamas commander in the Rafah Brigade, according to a statement from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz. More than 1,300 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed ‌in Gaza ⁠since the ceasefire took effect, according to the territory’s health officials, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Hamas does not usually disclose information about fatalities among its fighters.

articles.title: Guernsey charity gives alcohol consumption scorecard to residents
articles.summary: The Health Improvement Commission says it is to help people get a clearer picture of their intake.
articles.body:
An alcohol consumption campaign with scorecards to monitor units, is aimed at helping islanders make informed decisions about their health.

The Rethink Your Drink scheme, set up by the Health Improvement Commission for Guernsey and Alderney, encourages residents to fill in scorecards noting their weekly alcohol intake and compare the results to the recommended guidelines.

The charity said islanders will receive a scorecard through their letterbox.

Andrea Nightingale, substance use lead at the Health Improvement Commission, said the scorecard was "a simple, interactive and engaging way to help people understand their intake".

The charity said the 2023 Wellbeing Survey found that 35.2% of adults aged 16 and over who drink alcohol reported consuming more than 14 units a week.

The UK Chief Medical Officers' low-risk drinking guidelines recommend men and women drink no more than 14 units per week, spread over three or more days, with at least two alcohol-free days each week.

The commission added alcohol units can be difficult to estimate, so the scorecard provides "a tried and tested tool" to help people calculate their weekly units and compare their results to the guidelines.

Nightingale said: "The scorecard is about helping people get a clearer picture of where they are today and giving them the confidence to think about where they would like to be tomorrow.

"Small changes really can add up to a big difference, and for many people, simply knowing their number could help them consider whether any changes might benefit their health and wellbeing."

articles.title: Japan now has more than 100,000 people who are 100 or older
articles.summary: The number of people ages 100 or older in Japan surpassed a record 100,000 this year, the latest government figures show, underscoring the country’s rapidly aging and declining population.
articles.body: TOKYO — The number of people ages 100 or older in Japan surpassed a record 100,000 this year, the latest government figures show, underscoring the country’s rapidly aging and declining population. The Health and Welfare Ministry statistics released Tuesday show Japan now has 107,677 centenarians, up 7,914 from the previous year and exceeding the 100,000 mark for the first time. Nearly 88% of them are women. Kyoto resident Fuyo Kishimoto was recently recognized as the oldest Japanese woman at age 114. Japan’s oldest man is 112-year-old Hikaru Kato from Kumamoto in southern Japan. The figures were released to mark this year’s Sept. 15 Respect the Aged day, when healthy and active centenarians are honored by the government with a letter from Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and a silver sake cup. “I’m very pleased that many people are living a long, healthy and active lives,” Health Minister Kenichiro Ueno told reporters Tuesday, citing progress in medical technology, healthy lifestyle and diet as contributing factors. Ueno noted the importance of maintaining a sustainable social security system as the population continues to age and decline. Many younger people, however, are not optimistic about their future. The National Institute of Population and Social Security Research last week released the results of a survey indicating that more than 20% of both men and women who are single and between the ages of 18 and 34 have no intention of ever marrying, with nearly half saying they see no benefit in marriage. Ueno acknowledged that the reasons for marriage reluctance among young people include the high costs of raising and educating children and the mental and physical burden on working parents. He said the government would continue addressing their concerns and attempt to turn around problems related to Japan’s aging population and dwindling births. Japan’s drastic population decline is inevitable, experts say, noting the country’s total fertility rate dropped to a record low 1.14 in 2025, far below the 2.1 children needed to be born to each Japanese woman to maintain the current population. Japan’s total population during the 2020 census stood at 126 million, almost 30% of which were 65 or older. Experts estimate there will be a decline to 87 million by 2070, with nearly 40% ages 65 or older, according to the national institute. There were 153 people ages 100 or older in Japan when centenarian surveys began in 1963. They exceeded 1,000 in 1981 and surpassed 10,000 in 1998, according to the Health and Welfare Ministry.

articles.summary: USS Abraham Lincoln heads home after downing 200 Iranian drones, but four critical upgrades face White House resistance ahead of a China showdown.
articles.body: The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln is heading for home port in San Diego, while USS George H. W. Bush and USS George Washington remain on station in the North Arabian Gulf executing strikes and upholding the steel wall naval blockade. America’s aircraft carriers are more important than ever, and Lincoln and her crew of 5,000 will get a warm welcome. But, back in Washington, D.C., stormy weather is brewing for the carrier fleet. And one rogue wave coming directly from the White House could imperil the Navy in a future fight against China. First, a shout-out to Lincoln's combat success in the Middle East, including taking out 200 Iranian drones threatening commercial shipping. And oh yes, the Iranians tried and failed to target the Lincoln. "Since we’ve gotten here, and during Operation Epic Fury, the Iranians were looking for opportunities to attack this ship," Captain Daniel J. Keeler, commander of the Lincoln, told CNN in a hangar deck interview in July. "We’re very well-defended," said. Iran’s shots "don’t get close." USS GEORGE WASHINGTON CAPTAIN SAYS MORALE IS HIGH FOR NEW MIDEAST MISSION Brilliantly as they’ve performed, it’s high time for some major upgrades to naval aviation to prepare the force to take on China’s navy. First to arrive will be the MQ-25 Stingray refueling and reconnaissance drone. With wings that spread to 75 feet unfolded, the Stingray’s job is to deliver fuel from its orbiting post 1,000 miles away from the carrier, and to stay aloft for hours. Look for smaller wingman collaborative combat aircraft drones with extra weapons and electronic spectrum warfare effects to join the air wing in the future, too. The sky’s the limit for carrier-based drones on ships with adjustable catapults. President Donald Trump understands the value of carriers, yet he’s worried for years about the new catapults — where magnets instead of steam shoot planes down the deck. Ford has proven the new electromagnetic system with over 12,200 launches just from their most recent 326-day deployment. Combat data on the new "cats" looks good. Here’s something else you need to know: the magnetic catapults recharge faster than steam. Ford ran an all-out, multi-day surge exercise earlier this year, and the air wing was able to generate 25% more sorties with the new catapults, compared to the old steam type. "I think there’s overwhelming support in Congress and in the Pentagon for moving forward with EMALS," Senator Roger Wicker, chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said on Aug. 18. Ripping out combat-proven catapults and weapons elevators will slow shipyards and leave the U.S. Navy short of aircraft carriers to fight China. Also, there’s no going back. The aircraft carrier industrial base includes over 2,000 firms, many of them small businesses, across America. Switch the design of major systems, and you are looking at years of churn and delay. By the way, France ordered the new system for their next aircraft carrier, and China’s already building their own electromagnetic system, which they probably stole from us. Faster elevators. Not for the crew, they have up and down ladders. I’m talking about advanced weapons elevators. Made in Cincinnati, the new weapons elevators on Ford are rated for 24,000 lbs. instead of 12,000 lbs. for the old type, and they move 50% faster. Lower stage elevators move ordnance from the magazines in the aft and forward sections of the carrier while upper stage elevators lift the bombs and missiles up to the flight deck. All vital when the crew is rearming aircraft during combat operations. Once again, the White House is wavering, but consider that the Navy’s newest long-range weapons are big and heavy. The Malice air-to-air missile, unveiled just last month, weighs 1500 lbs. Best to stick with the advanced weapons elevators. PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION A stealthy new fighter jet. Long in the works, the Navy’s sixth-generation F/A-XX is ready to move ahead. Boeing and Northrop Grumman both have secret demonstrator planes. The new fighter-bomber is crucial to adding more range for carrier strike operations. Besides, the clock is ticking. Production of the mainstay Navy F/A-18EF Superhornet is shutting down, and China’s already flown two sixth-generation aircraft prototypes, including one for their navy. Congress instructed the Pentagon to pick a winner and get moving, so point your finger at the Department of War for the delay. articles.title: What to know about the victims of the NBC L.A. news helicopter crash
articles.summary: Tributes began pouring in Wednesday after a deadly news helicopter crash in Los Angeles left three people dead.
articles.body: Tributes began pouring in Wednesday after a deadly news helicopter crash in Los Angeles left three people dead. The crash occurred just before 7p.m. local time on Tuesday in the Chatsworth area of the San Fernando Valley, as the news chopper was covering a separate road traffic accident. Angel City Air operated the helicopter, which was affiliated with NBC Los Angeles. The victims aboard the helicopter were identified as Eliana Moreno, a journalist familiar to viewers of the station and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52, and pilot George Marciniw. The pair began flying together in 2023. A pedestrian on the ground was also confirmed to have died at the scene, officials said. Authorities have yet to identify the individual. Zareh Sevanesian, who witnessed the crash, said the helicopter was swaying before it started losing altitude. “It was just getting lower and lower and lower and lower,” he said on NBC’s “TODAY” show. Eliana Moreno Moreno, in her late 30s, was born in Orange County, south of L.A. She graduated from Chapman University in the area with a degree in broadcast journalism and political science in 2010, NBC Los Angeles reported. Moreno joined Angel City Air’s helicopter team the same year and has reported for multiple Southern California news outlets. A seasoned aerial journalist who also reported in Spanish, Moreno was known on her official Instagram account as, “Eli in the heli,” due to her work. There, she shared pictures of her chickens and pet dogs and a video of her engagement to fiancée Robert Barrientos, in 2025. He did not immediately respond to NBC News’s request for comment. The pair ran a half-marathon together in May, after which she wrote: “I surpassed everything I thought I could ever do so let’s see what I do next!” Moreno also frequently shared multiple images of herself in the news chopper, covering stories on the go, with one caption reading, “I have the best job in the world.” Veteran NBC4 Los Angeles anchor Colleen Williams paid tribute to “dear colleagues” while on air Tuesday evening. Visibly emotional, she told viewers: “We are coming on the air with heavy hearts tonight because we lost valued friends and colleagues ... while on assignment tonight.” “We are going to take a couple of minutes to think about that, process it,” she added, her voice shaking. Lynette Romero, co-anchor of NBC L.A.’s morning newscast, said they were “heartbroken” and are thinking of the families of Moreno and Marciniw. “They were both doing what they loved so much, and for me, that’s comfort in knowing how happy they were. They loved breaking news, and they loved being in News Chopper 4,” she said Wednesday on NBC’s “TODAY” show. George Marciniw Marciniw also grew up in southern California, where he graduated from Burbank High School in 1974, according to NBC L.A. Marciniw is believed to have had over 30 years of flight experience. He often shared sunsets and scenic pictures from the area on what he dubbed a “news cruise” in the helicopter. He often credited pictures on his official Instagram page to his companion and colleague, Moreno. “And that’s a wrap for Friday night as the heavy fog rolls in with Eliana Moreno,” he wrote, sharing an image of the chopper. In another, he posted a picture of the L.A. Dodgers stadium lit up brightly at night, captioned: “A few shots Eliana took as we flew over Dodgers after the game. “Go Dodgers.” Many online paid tribute to Marciniw, detailing his professionalism and fun-loving spirit. “Fly high in the great beyond,” wrote one individual. “Total utter disbelief,” wrote another. NBC Los Angeles and Telemundo 52 issued a joint statement expressing condolences for the pair. “We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening,” the stations said. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives.” The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration will begin investigating the cause of the helicopter crash.

articles.title: Paris court awards Kim Kardashian 1 euro after her 2016 robbery
articles.summary: A Paris court on Tuesday awarded 1 euro ($1.15) to Kim Kardashian for having been the victim of an armed robbery in the French capital in 2016, the amount of compensation she had asked for, according to a lawyer involved in the case.
articles.body: A Paris court on Tuesday awarded 1 euro ($1.15) to Kim Kardashian for having been the victim of an armed robbery in the French capital in 2016, the amount of compensation she had asked for, according to a lawyer involved in the case. Kardashian has sought to move on since the court last year found eight people guilty for their roles in what the celebrity described as “the most terrifying experience of my life.” She and stylist Simone Harouche expressed gratitude to the French justice system in a joint statement. “The experience was deeply traumatic, and its impact has stayed with us. Today’s decision is not about the compensation, but about accountability and recognition,” the statement to The Associated Press read. “We are thankful to the Court and everyone who supported us throughout this process, and we hope to now move forward and continue to heal.” The court awarded a former receptionist at the Hôtel de Pourtalès 109,516 euros ($126,472), according to his lawyer. Kardashian had been staying at the hotel when the robbery gang targeted her. The receptionist said he had been traumatized by the October 2, 2016 jewel heist during Fashion Week. He had sought 550,000 euros ($634,868) in damages and interest. His lawyer, Mohand Ouidja, welcomed the decision as a victory. The lawyer read the court’s written decisions pertaining to Kardashian and the others aloud to the AP. The court awarded the hotel 50,000 euros ($57,741). It awarded 1 euro — the amount she had requested — to Harouche, Kardashian’s stylist who was present during the robbery. French lawyers who acted for Kardashian during the trial didn’t respond to text messages and phone calls this week from the AP. Two of the robbers, dressed as police, forced their way into her suite, bound Kardashian with zip ties and tape and made off with more than $6 million in jewelry, including a diamond ring she’d worn that night to a Givenchy show. Because of their ages, the robbers became known in France as “les papys braqueurs,” or the grandpa robbers. Six of them were in their 60s and 70s when they were tried for armed robbery, kidnapping, gang association and other charges. With time already served in pretrial detention, none of those found guilty went back to prison. None of them appealed the verdict. Kardashian said in a statement issued after their conviction that she was “deeply grateful to the French authorities for pursuing justice in this case.” “The crime was the most terrifying experience of my life, leaving a lasting impact on me and my family,” the celebrity said. “While I’ll never forget what happened, I believe in the power of growth and accountability and pray for healing for all. I remain committed to advocating for justice and promoting a fair legal system.”

articles.title: Four US army Chinooks land at Land's End airport
articles.summary: The military helicopters, which made a stop off to refuel in Cornwall, were also seen in Jersey.
articles.body:
Four US army Chinook helicopters made a quick stop off at one of the UK's smallest commercial airports.

The tandem rotor military helicopters landed at Land's End Airport, Cornwall on Tuesday to refuel, before heading on to the Channel Islands.

The Isles of Scilly Steamship Group, which owns and operates the airport, said it believed the helicopters were part of US President Donald Trump's two day visit to Ireland , and were en route to Jersey.

Chris Pearson, manager of Land's End Airport, said it was an "incredible sight" as it had "never happened before and I can't imagine it will happen again."

The airport which is just a few miles from Land's End, primarily connects Cornwall with the Isles of Scilly, using smaller Twin Otter aircrafts.

Pearson added: "It's not every day you see one Chinook at Land's End Airport, let alone four - it was a real privilege to welcome them.

"These are enormous helicopters, and seeing four arriving together at our airport at the very western tip of Cornwall was an incredible sight.

"The visit highlights the unique versatility of Land's End Airport - we may be small, but we can certainly hold our own alongside much larger airports."

The Chinooks also landed in Jersey on Tuesday before leaving the next day.

articles.title: EU announces plan to ban social media for under 13s
articles.summary: The European Union is moving to ban social media for kids under 13 and impose restrictions on the digital technology for older children, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced Wednesday.
articles.body: The European Union is moving to ban social media for under 13s across the bloc and impose restrictions on the digital technology for older children, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced Wednesday. The move to develop EU-wide rules comes after several individual EU member states have introduced social media limits on teenagers amid a global push to restrict children’s access to social media. Australia became the first country in the world to ban social media for under 16s in December 2025. “No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15,” Von der Leyen said during her state of the union address in Strasbourg, France. The EU would allow 13- and 14-year olds to have “mini accounts” with parental supervision and limited features, she added. The use of such accounts would be capped at one hour per day. Most major social media platforms already say they ban children under the age of 13, but lawmakers and online safety experts have questioned whether they have adequate measures in place to enforce that rule. The European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, would on Thursday propose a new Kids Act, Von der Leyen said. Under the act, the bloc would reverse the burden of proof, such that social media platforms would have to prove that they are safe for minors. “I am aware that many perceive the power of big tech as overwhelming and impossible to roll back. I disagree,” Von der Leyen said. “Europe has the power to act. It is us who decide the rules, not Big Tech.” In reality, the Kids Act could take years to cross the line, as it will need to be approved by individual EU member states, several of which have already pushed ahead with their own social media bans. France became the first EU country to ban social media for children under the age of 15, following a vote by French lawmakers in July. The ban was later struck down by the country’s Constitutional Court, however. Spain, Denmark and Sweden are among other EU countries pursuing age restrictions on social media use. Lauro Fava a partner at law firm Pinsent Masons said the EU Kids Act would “be a new EU behemoth” comparable to the existing Digital Services Act, which regulates large online platforms, and the AI Act. “For affected companies, they will be able to comply with a single, coherent, and potentially more balanced rulebook than if they had to deal with a multitude of member state laws,” he wrote in a commentary Tuesday after the EU-wide online safety measures were trailed in media reports. On AI, Von der Leyen said she was optimistic that artificial intelligence had the potential to “benefit humanity if we get it right.” However, “massive risks” associated with the technology – including “hacking on a level we never thought possible,” needed to be addressed in order to unlock the technology’s potential, she added. Von der Leyen said she would invite the leading AI labs for talks on how the European Union can support the industry’s efforts to slow down the technology’s development – something the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI have all called for in recent days. – Clare Duffy contributed to this report.

articles.title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
articles.summary: Thaci, 58, was sentenced to 25 years in prison for ‌crimes including murder, torture and illegal detention.
articles.body:
The Kosovo war crimes tribunal has convicted former Kosovar President Hashim Thaci of four counts of war crimes committed during his country’s war for independence from Serbia.

Thaci, 58, was sentenced on Wednesday to 25 years in prison for ‌crimes, including murder, torture and illegal detention, committed as top commander of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the ⁠territory’s violent break ⁠from Serbia in the 1990s.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers (KSC) in The Hague, Netherlands, said he was ⁠guilty of the murder ⁠of 96 political ⁠opponents and perceived collaborators with Serbian security forces by the KLA during the conflict.

Wearing a suit and tie, he stood in silence as Presiding Judge Charles Smith read out the sentence.

Three former KLA senior commanders were also sentenced for several different charges.

Jakup Krasniqi was sentenced to 25 years in prison, Kadri Veseli was given 18 years, including the time he spent in custody, and Rexhep Selimi was sentenced to 13 years, including the time spent in custody.

The verdict stated that they would have the right to appeal.

The four men were acquitted on six charges of crimes against humanity because the judges said the prosecutors failed to prove that crimes were committed as part of a widespread and systematic attack on civilians.

The trial has been controversial within Kosovo as many Kosovan Albanians see the KLA and Thaci as revered figures because of their role in the 1998-99 independence war.

Kosovo’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Glauk Konjufca condemned the verdict as “terrible and harmful to Kosovo”.

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama reacted on social media to the verdict by releasing an illustration of The Hague with the Albanian word, “Marre”, which translates to “shame” or “disgrace”.

In Kosovo’s capital, Pristina, thousands of people watched the reading of the verdict live on a huge screen and were stunned at the sentence. Some started shouting slogans in support of the KLA and Thaci.

Serbia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Interior Ivica Dacic called the verdicts a “warning” to Pristina “that a fake state cannot be built on mass graves of murdered Serbs”.

He said that the conviction represents a “clear, and albeit belated, confirmation of what Serbia and the Serbian people have been saying loudly for more than a quarter of a century – that the so-called KLA was a criminal and terrorist organization”.

The KLA first emerged in the mid 1990s, but its armed operations intensified in 1997 and 1998.

Serbian forces responded with several large police and military operations, leading to a full-blown war in 1999, which resulted in the deaths of an estimated of 13,000 people and the displacement of hundreds of thousands.

During the war, Thaci was one of the heads of the KLA’s political and information directorate. Once the war ended, he became Kosovo’s prime minister and foreign minister and then served as president from 2016 to 2020.

Thaci resigned in November 2020, after he was indicted by the tribunal. He and the other convicted commanders were transferred to detention in The Hague in November of that year.

Reporting from The Hague, Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego said the verdicts come as Kosovo is facing “political deadlock”.

“There have been repeated elections to try and get some form of stable government so they can get some kind of closer relationship with the European Union going, but there have been repeated blocks to that, and failures to form that government,” she said.

“This is just going to be another stumbling block on that path to stability.”

Gallego also said the verdict “cuts right to the bone” for many Kosovar Albanians, who view Thaci as a heroic figure.

“Closure is not in the immediate future. There has already been a very angry response in Pristina from thousands of Kosovar Albanians there about this judgement,” she explained.

“It cannot be understated really how abject a decision this is for Kosovar Albanians who see Hashem Thaci as not just the country’s former president, but also a symbol of Kosovo’s liberation.”

“Not all crimes seem to be treated equally by the courts” said Jeta Xharra, the director of the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network in Kosovo, who told Al Jazeera that the day marked more injustice for the Albanian majority of Kosovo.

“Serbian forces were involved in the killing of over 10,000 civilians, many of them women and children, yet majority members of the Serbian forces have not been held accountable for these crimes. And today, we see very lengthy sentences handed down to four members of the KLA,” she said.

Xharra said that people in Kosovo could not forget the terror they had experienced before the war, when they were treated as second-class citizens simply because they belonged to a different ethnic group.

“This court was seen as a court trying one ethnicity only, Kosovo Albanians. While that is not how the war was in Kosovo, majority of the crimes were committed by Serbian forces. Of course, all victims must get justice but this particular court is making sure that one side only is being tried”, she told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Burnham thanks well-wishers following his father's death
articles.summary: All opposition leaders sent condolences to Burnham as he cancelled engagements earlier this week.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has thanked party leaders for their support following the death of his father, Roy, on Monday.

All opposition leaders sent condolences to him as he cancelled engagements earlier this week.

Burnham had previously spoken about the fact his dad did not know he had become prime minister, due to his advanced Alzheimer's.

Posting on social media, he thanked "everyone who has shared a kind message about my dad, particularly the leaders of the other parties".

Burnham added: "My family and I have been helped though this difficult time by people's warmth and compassion. It means a great deal to us and we wanted to say thank you."

Speaking to journalists on his first day back at work on Wednesday, Burnham thanked all those who had sent "so many lovely messages" to him and his family.

"It's hard and it will be hard for a little while but better to get back to the job," he said.

"I also want to thank the leaders of the other parties, all of whom sent a message, and it shows there is decency in British politics still and that's lovely to see, so thank you from us all, the whole family.

"But my dad would want me to be back out there bringing some of the changes that he always pushed me to make."

He has described how his father, a former telephone engineer, had raised him with "laughter, love and support" alongside his mother Eileen in Culcheth, Cheshire.

In July, Burnham spoke about his father's condition and said it had influenced his drive to reform adult social care in England.

articles.title: Trump envoy secures release of 25 Belarus prisoners as U.S. drops more sanctions
articles.summary: Belarus has agreed to free 25 prisoners in return for a further easing of U.S. sanctions, an envoy for President Donald Trump said on Wednesday.
articles.body: Belarus has agreed to free 25 prisoners in return for a further easing of U.S. sanctions, an envoy for President Donald Trump said on Wednesday. The deal was part of lengthy negotiations, under way since last year, in which Washington is urging Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko to free hundreds of people including human rights campaigners, political activists, journalists and lawyers in return for sanctions relief. The process is sensitive because Lukashenko, a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, has long been shunned by the West for repressing his opponents and supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine. European Union sanctions against Belarus remain firmly in place. “We agreed to an interim deal, and as a show of goodwill Belarus will release 25 people and in exchange the United States will lift sanctions on two companies,” Trump’s envoy, John Coale, told reporters in the Belarusian capital Minsk. The figure of 25 releases was much lower than the 250 that Coale negotiated when he last visited Minsk in March. However, the American said both sides would work to resolve outstanding issues to pave the way for more prisoners to go free and further sanctions to be removed. “We will continue to improve US-Belarus relations and are working to secure the release of more people in the very near future. We are not finished!” he posted later on X. Exiled Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said the 25 had been safely brought to neighboring Lithuania. Among those released, according to human rights group Viasna, were prominent journalist Andrei Alyaksandrau, who was serving a 14-year term, and his wife Iryna Zlobina, sentenced to nine years. Authorities also freed Liudmila Chekina, head of the independent news portal TUT.BY, which was shut down in 2021. She had been serving a 12-year term. A source familiar with the situation told Reuters that, in addition to the 25, a significant number of prisoners were expected to be freed and remain inside Belarus. Viasna said relatives of some detainees had been told they could collect their loved ones from penal colonies on Wednesday morning. Viasna, which is banned in Belarus, says the former Soviet state still held more than 900 political prisoners as of the start of this week, even after Coale negotiated the release of hundreds since the middle of last year. Among the most frequent charges against them are “extremist” activity, conspiring to seize power, incitement to hatred, or insulting the president. At Tuesday’s talks with Coale, Lukashenko denied the people in question were political prisoners and rejected assertions by rights groups and the exiled opposition that he is steadily arresting more people to replace those he releases. The two companies to be removed from U.S. sanctions are Lakokraska, a manufacturer of paints and industrial coatings, and Bellesbumprom, a state-owned industrial concern that oversees the forestry, pulp and paper sectors. Sanctions against them had been in place since 2008 and 2023, respectively. Coale also promised Lukashenko on Tuesday to get U.S. banks to hand back tens of millions of dollars in frozen Belarusian assets. Coale’s efforts since last year have led to the release, among many others, of Nobel Peace Prize winner Ales Bialiatski and leading opposition figures. His diplomacy has earned gratitude from many Belarusians, but human rights groups and opposition politicians say arrests continue and Lukashenko has yet to end repression in the country. “Today, alongside our joy for those released, we remember those who remain behind bars,” Tsikhanouskaya posted on X. “There are hundreds of them. Behind every number is a person, their family, and their loved ones who continue to wait.”

articles.title: Coffee lovers have a new No. 1 city and it's not Portland or Seattle
articles.summary: Orlando topped WalletHub's ranking of best coffee cities in the US, beating Portland and Seattle thanks to affordable shops and free Wi-Fi access.
articles.body: The country's best city for coffee lovers is not Seattle, Portland or even New York, according to a new report. Best known for its area theme parks, Orlando, Florida, has been brewing up a new attraction as America's top destination for coffee lovers, a WalletHub analysis found. The City Beautiful took the No. 1 spot in WalletHub's ranking of the 100 largest U.S. cities, edging out Portland, Oregon, which fell from first place last year to No. 2. COFFEE LOVERS CAN TAKE HEART: UP TO 5 CUPS A DAY APPEARS SAFE FOR MOST ADULTS, EXPERTS SAY Miami ranked No. 3, followed by Long Beach, California, at No. 4 and Seattle, the birthplace of Starbucks, at No. 5. The results offer a new definition of what makes a great coffee city today. While coffee is a daily habit for 66% of Americans, according to the National Coffee Association, coffee drinkers are increasingly looking for affordable, reliable, highly rated shops that have free Wi-Fi instead of trendy cafés. Coffee shops increasingly serve as workspaces and social hubs for tourists, students and remote workers, WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo, based in South Carolina, told Fox News Digital. AMERICA'S BEST FOOD CITIES RANKED BY EXPERT, WITH CHOICES THAT COULD INFURIATE LOCALS Lupo said Orlando's tourism-driven economy means visitors often need a reliable place to charge their phones, connect to free Wi-Fi and save money where they can. "People want to have a coffee, they may want to go in and scroll for a little while before they hit Disney World, so they want to make the rest of the experience as affordable as they can to spend more of their money on the tourist attraction," Lupo said. Orlando is also home to the University of Central Florida, he added. "There's a lot of broke college kids out there and they're already spending the little money they have on coffee, so they don't want to have to pay for the Wi-Fi also." LOOKING FOR BETTER COFFEE? HUNDREDS OF CHEFS AND SOMMELIERS SAY THESE ARE THE WORLD'S BEST Cities that attract young adults and college students also ranked highly, including Pittsburgh at No. 9 and Austin, Texas, at No. 10. Pittsburgh's growing med-tech and tech sectors have helped draw young professionals to the city, Lupo said. Lupo was most surprised that this year's ranking included three Florida cities in its top 10. Tampa landed at No. 6. "You have three cities in Florida — hot, muggy, warm weather pretty much year-round — and also you have Long Beach, a Southern California city," he said, adding that they could be opting for an iced coffee. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "Maybe that's how a lot of folks start off their day, drinking a cold iced coffee first thing in the morning." Of the 100 cities WalletHub examined, it measured "coffee friendliness," including the price of packaged coffee and cappuccinos, household coffee spending, the share of residents with coffee makers and the number of coffee shops per capita. The personal finance company also weighed the availability of affordable coffee shops that have at least 4.5-star reviews, free Wi-Fi, coffee and tea manufacturers, doughnut shops and local interest based on Google searches. In cities such as New York, rising coffee prices and pressure on small, independent shops may help explain why the Big Apple landed at No. 44, Lupo said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES The ranking also underscores how a daily coffee habit affects the wallet. Households in the most coffee-crazy cities can spend up to $327 a year on the beverage, while frequent espresso and cappuccino drinkers may save by preparing drinks at home, WalletHub found. Lupo noted that several lower-ranked cities, including Laredo, Texas; Toledo, Ohio; Detroit; Memphis, Tennessee; and Lubbock, Texas, are places where residents may have less room in their budgets for coffee purchases. "When grocery costs are at a premium, usually one of the first places you'll cut back [is] things like coffee," he said. Buying a coffee or espresso machine for home can "pretty much pay for itself in the first couple of months," Lupo added. articles.title: Gold mine collapses in Sudan: At least 67 workers killed, many more feared trapped
articles.summary: Rest of World News: At least 67 people have been killed since a gold mine collapsed at Al-Nuhud town in Sudan's West Kordofan on Sunday, with many more still missing and .
articles.body: At least 67 people have been killed since a gold mine collapsed at Al-Nuhud town in Sudan's West Kordofan on Sunday, with many more still missing and feared dead beneath the rubble.According to locals cited by the Reuters and AFP news agencies, the high death toll at tht Al-Zaraa mine was due to the the absence of safety procedures or rescue equipment at the makeshift wells, when the shafts collapsed."The shafts here are all close together, if one collapses, it brings down all the ones next to it", said Al-Amin Suleiman, a miner."There are people still trapped underground since yesterday. I don't think they are alive", he added.One of the survivors, Khair al-Sayyed Jabara, told AFP that an all-night rescue operation was carried out by his fellow miners using the same rudimentary tools they use to mine."We don't know how many more are still inside," he said. "Everyone's working very hard to retrieve the bodies or any survivors, but it's difficult. We need heavy machinery to clear the rock and soil."The West Kordofan, along with the neighbouring Darfur region, is under the control of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a force accused of genocide in Darfur. Despite having declared a parallel government, the RSF's governing capabilities remain limited, and people in western Sudan remain largely dependent on aid and local community networks for survival.Sudan is one of Africa's largest gold producers, but the vast majority of its gold is extracted through dangerous artisanal mining techniques before being smuggled out of the country.Since war broke out in April 2023 between Sudan's army and the RSF, the war efforts of both sides have been largely funded by the gold industry, alongside foreign backers. West Kordofan, under RSF control, is a key source of revenue for the paramilitary force through gold mining.The conflict has devastated Sudan's already fragile economy and left much of the country out of work, driving many people into a dangerous gold rush. Even before the war pushed nearly 20 million Sudanese into severe hunger, artisanal mining employed more than two million people, according to industry figures.Nearly all of the gold smuggled or exported from Sudan is routed through the United Arab Emirates, the world's second-largest gold exporter. The UAE denies widespread reports that it arms the RSF.Sudan is one of the continent's top gold producers, having recorded a "five-year high" of 70 tonnes of production last year, according to official figures. However, officials say most of this gold is smuggled across Sudan's borders , including through Chad, South Sudan and Egypt, before reaching the UAE.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
